what_its_for: Fosfomycin is an antibiotic used to treat uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs) — also called bladder infections — in women. It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection. It is most commonly used for infections caused by E. coli or Enterococcus faecalis.
how_to_take: Fosfomycin comes as a powder packet that you mix with water and drink. Open one packet and pour the powder into 3 to 4 ounces (about 90 to 120 mL) of cool water — do not use hot water. Stir well until the powder is completely dissolved, then drink the entire mixture right away. You can take it with or without food. Do not take it as a dry powder — always mix it with water first.
dosing: For most adults, the usual dose is one packet (3 grams) taken as a single dose — meaning you only take it one time. Do not take a second packet unless your doctor specifically tells you to. One dose is usually enough to treat an uncomplicated bladder infection.
missed_dose: Because fosfomycin is almost always taken as just one single dose, a missed dose is unlikely. However, if your doctor prescribed more than one dose and you forget to take one, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue as directed. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store the unopened powder packets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep all packets in a dry place and out of reach of children. Do not use a packet if it appears damaged or if the expiration date has passed.
what_to_avoid: Avoid skipping your dose or stopping treatment early, even if you feel better quickly. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking any other medications, vitamins, or supplements at the same time, as some products may reduce how well fosfomycin works. In particular, let your doctor know if you are taking metoclopramide (Reglan), as it can lower the effectiveness of fosfomycin.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if: your symptoms (burning, frequent urination, painful urination) do not start to improve within 2 to 3 days after taking fosfomycin; your symptoms get worse; you develop a fever, chills, back or side pain, or nausea and vomiting (these may be signs of a kidney infection); you experience a severe skin rash, itching, or signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; you develop severe or ongoing diarrhea, which could be a sign of a gut infection called C. difficile.
when_it_works: Many people start to feel better within 24 to 48 hours after taking fosfomycin. However, it is important to give the medication a full 2 to 3 days to work. If you are not feeling better after 2 to 3 days, contact your doctor. Your doctor may want to do a urine test to make sure the antibiotic is working against the bacteria causing your infection.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Fosfomycin is sometimes used during pregnancy, but only under close medical supervision. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of fosfomycin may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before taking this medication if you are breastfeeding. Kidney disease: If you have kidney problems, tell your doctor before taking fosfomycin, as it may not be recommended or the dose may need to be adjusted. Children: The safety and effectiveness of this medication has not been well established in children under 12 years old. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Your doctor will decide if this medication is right for you.
